headline: Highest risk is medium: MinerU’s MCP/API surfaces can ingest ComfyUI-generated content, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways; no direct shared-write or residency breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can emit generated images/workflows, and MinerU exposes an MCP Server plus API surfaces that may ingest those outputs. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if MinerU treats extracted content as trusted. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are passed into MinerU through the MCP Server or API
IF MinerU parses embedded text or metadata as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted ComfyUI outputs
Strip metadata and prompts from generated assets before handoff
Add a provenance tag to all ComfyUI outputs
Review MinerU parsing rules for instruction-like text
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation between generation and extraction

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are documented as offline or allowlisted, and neither profile shows filesystem read/write or secrets handling. ComfyUI touches local model assets; MinerU processes local documents. A leakage path is possible only if the operator manually moves sensitive files between them, so blast radius is limited and not default.
conditions: IF the operator manually transfers sensitive documents or images from ComfyUI into MinerU
IF MinerU is configured to upload extracted content beyond its allowlisted egress
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of the shared workflow
Use separate directories for model assets and documents
Verify MinerU egress allowlist before processing
Redact secrets from prompts and source files
requires-engineering: add per-job data-class tagging

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, while MinerU also lacks filesystem write and git mutation. MinerU does support MCP and concurrent inference, but there is no overlapping mutable resource shown, so direct capability conflict is limited to coordination overhead rather than destructive contention.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external mutable resource through MCP or an API wrapper
IF an orchestrator adds shared state not shown in either profile
mitigations: Run the agents in separate job queues
Avoid shared mutable backends
Serialize access in the orchestrator
Monitor for duplicate task execution
requires-engineering: add resource locks around shared APIs

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU can consume API/MCP inputs, so ComfyUI outputs could become MinerU inputs without a documented verification step. If generated text or OCR-like artifacts are treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream extraction or actions. The pair lacks an explicit validation bridge, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF MinerU ingests ComfyUI outputs as source documents or annotations
IF downstream workflows trust MinerU extraction without human review
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require confidence thresholds before downstream use
Compare MinerU output against the original source
Log provenance for each extracted field
requires-engineering: add verification gates in the workflow

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or PHI-handling mismatch is documented for either open-source profile. ComfyUI and MinerU both present offline/self-isolated operation, and the evidence bundle is empty, so there is no basis for a compliance breach finding beyond speculation.
conditions: IF a deployment adds regulated data classes not shown in either profile
IF an operator routes data into a jurisdictional environment with stricter rules
mitigations: Document the data classes in scope
Confirm local retention settings
Separate regulated and unregulated workflows
Review deployment jurisdiction
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance assessment
